title: Mental Health Care Plans for Asian Communities in Australia
description: Understand mental health care plans in Australia, prepare for a GP visit and ask questions to find a therapist who understands your cultural context.
author: Sonia Kaurah
article_html:
Quick answers

What are mental health care plans?

You develop a mental health care plan with your GP. It can support referral for psychological treatment if your GP assesses that a plan and referral are appropriate for your needs.

Does a mental health care plan make therapy free?

A mental health care plan does not mean appointments will be free. Ask the practice whether Medicare applies to your practitioner and appointment, and confirm the fee, applicable rebate and amount you would pay.

How can you assess a therapist’s cultural understanding?

Ask prospective therapists how they would account for your values, language preferences and circumstances, such as family expectations or migration experience. Listen for specific answers about their approach and questions about your own experience.

In this article

  1. A Care Plan Is a Starting Point
  2. How Do Mental Health Care Plans Work?
  3. How Can You Find a Therapist Who Understands Your Culture?
  4. Where to Ask About Local Services
  5. References

A Care Plan Is a Starting Point

We recommend discussing a mental health care plan with your GP while separately asking prospective therapists how they would understand your cultural context. A care plan can be a doorway into care, but it does not describe the conversation inside.

This guide concerns ongoing care, not urgent support. If life is in danger, call 000. Lifeline offers crisis support on 13 11 14 at any time, in English (Lifeline crisis support - 13 11 14).

How Do Mental Health Care Plans Work?

A plan is developed with your GP and can support a referral for psychological treatment. Before the appointment, think about what has been troubling you and how it affects daily life. Describe any cultural or language preferences you want considered in a referral. This helps explain the support you are seeking; your GP assesses whether a plan and referral are appropriate.

Foundation Psychology’s FAQ describes access to up to 10 individual therapy sessions per calendar year (Mental Health Care Plans FAQs by Doctors - Foundation Psychology Melbourne). Further sessions can involve a GP review or a further referral letter, depending on the circumstances. Confirm your current eligibility, remaining sessions and referral requirements with your GP before relying on that allowance.

A care plan does not mean appointments will be free. Before booking, ask the practice whether Medicare applies to the particular practitioner and appointment you are considering. Ask for the session fee, any applicable rebate and the amount you would pay after that rebate. Do not assume Medicare applies because someone uses the title therapist, counsellor or coach. Consider cost alongside cultural understanding when choosing whom to see.

How Can You Find a Therapist Who Understands Your Culture?

Start by deciding what cultural understanding would mean for you. You might prioritise a particular language or dialect, shared heritage, faith, migration experience or understanding of family expectations. Choose what is relevant to your life rather than treating any background as a shared experience.

Ask your GP for practitioner options and read practice biographies for explicitly stated languages and relevant experience. Contact the practice about anything unclear. Do not infer ethnicity, language or competence from a name or photograph.

Ask How They Would Work With Your Cultural Context

Ask about their experience with the circumstances you describe. Find out how they would account for your values and respond when they misunderstand something. If language is a priority, ask which language sessions can be conducted in and whether other language support is available.

Look for specific explanations and questions about your individual experience. Do not rely on a cultural competence label alone. Use the conversation to decide whether to book, ask further questions or contact another practitioner.

Where to Ask About Local Services

If you are unsure where to look, healthdirect’s Mental health helplines page lists Medicare Mental Health, which offers advice and connections to local mental health services. Explain what you are seeking and ask about local options.

About the author

Sonia Kaurah

Founder & CEO - Tala Thrive | Ex VC | Board Member | Building Culturally Competent Mental Health Care | Rising Star 2024 Award Winner | Public Speaker

References

  1. Mental health helplines | healthdirect
  2. Lifeline crisis support - 13 11 14
  3. Mental Health Care Plans FAQs by Doctors - Foundation Psychology Melbourne
  4. Mental Health Care Plan: Get Support
  5. Medicare Mental Health Care Plan
  6. Better Access to Mental Health Care initiative under Medicare | APS

This article is general information and should be adapted to your circumstances.

summary: Understand mental health care plans in Australia, prepare for a GP visit and ask questions to find a therapist who understands your cultural context.

summary_items.label: What are mental health care plans?
summary_items.description: You develop a mental health care plan with your GP. It can support referral for psychological treatment if your GP assesses that a plan and referral are appropriate for your needs.

summary_items.label: Does a mental health care plan make therapy free?
summary_items.description: A mental health care plan does not mean appointments will be free. Ask the practice whether Medicare applies to your practitioner and appointment, and confirm the fee, applicable rebate and amount you would pay.

summary_items.label: How can you assess a therapist’s cultural understanding?
summary_items.description: Ask prospective therapists how they would account for your values, language preferences and circumstances, such as family expectations or migration experience. Listen for specific answers about their approach and questions about your own experience.
